text:
maria.support: FYI ACME (acme-inc) reports a sharp p99 regression on streaming responses to /v1/chat/stream — TTFB looks the same but total time spikes ~2-3x. Started ~2026-03-15T18:20Z. Request id examples: r-8f3a2b, r-8f3a2c.

anna.csm: Customer says non-streaming responses are fine, only streaming path impacted. They're noticing UX stuck on 'loading' until final flush.

maria.support: Repro (customer):
```bash
# streaming (curl + chunked)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-open","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"short"}]}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream

# non-streaming
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-open","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"short"}]}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat"

jake.runtime: On it. Looking at metrics: streaming.total_latency_p99 jumped from ~600ms -> ~2.4s since 17:40Z. streaming.first_byte_p99 stayed ~110-140ms. That pattern points to trailing-chunk/flush delays, not model compute.

kevin.sre: Any infra changes around 17:30-18:00Z?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out proxy-write-coalesce v2 to us-west1 at 2026-03-15T17:45:12Z (change: increased write coalesce window from 1ms -> 8ms to reduce small writes).

jake.runtime: That's likely it. Increasing coalescing can add tail latency for small final writes (especially streaming where many tokens are tiny writes). I'll run a local repro with coalesce=8ms.

maria.support: Customer logs show many streams finishing with a tiny trailing chunk (1-5 bytes) that waits 50-200ms before being flushed. Example: 
```
[2026-03-15T18:22:01.123Z] request=r-8f3a2b status=streaming stage=flush size=2 delay_ms=183
[2026-03-15T18:22:01.310Z] request=r-8f3a2c status=streaming stage=flush size=1 delay_ms=92
```

jake.runtime: Reproduced locally: with coalesce=8ms streaming.total_p99 ~= 2.1s; with coalesce=1ms it's ~620ms. Plan: rollback the proxy coalesce change for streaming routes in us-west1 as a hotfix and add an immediate feature flag to bypass coalescing for content-type text/event-stream. Will rollout in ~15m.

kevin.sre: I'll trigger rollback and patch LB rules to target the old proxy config for /v1/chat/stream paths. Also enabling TCP keepalive tweaks to avoid delayed-ack interactions while rollback happens.

ops-bot: ops-bot: rollback started for proxy-write-coalesce v2 in us-west1 at 2026-03-15T18:35:00Z (canary).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback completed in us-west1 at 2026-03-15T18:40:12Z. Canary OK -> full.

maria.support: ACME reports improvement within minutes: p99 down to ~650ms and UI no longer stuck. Customer confirms UX is back to normal. :white_check_mark:

jake.runtime: Follow-ups: 1) add per-tenant flush-ms override (default 1ms for streaming) 2) telemetry: emit per-request trailing_chunk_delay_ms and coalesce_delay_ms 3) add alert: streaming.total_latency_p99 > 1s for 10m -> page. I'll open PRs and a small-runbook.

anna.csm: Customer asked if we can make a permanent exception for their tenant until we ship per-tenant setting. Can we do a short-lived config toggle?

kevin.sre: Yes, we can set a tenant-level rule in the proxy config for acme-inc to always use coalesce=1ms. I'll apply and note in incident doc.

kevin.sre: Created incident doc: https://go/incident/INC-2026-1234 (owner=jake.runtime). Postmortem and action items assigned.

maria.support: Closing loop with ACME. Will monitor p95/p99 for next 24h and follow up with timeline for per-tenant control. Thanks all. :pray:
